items.name: Post-Wagnerian chromaticism at the breaking point
items.description: Schoenberg takes Wagner's chromatic language and pushes it further: longer stretches of harmonic ambiguity, more complex chromatic voice-leading, more deferred resolution. The tonality is still presen

items.name: Extreme emotional intensity — Expressionist temperature
items.description: The late Romantic Schoenberg is emotionally overwrought by intention: enormous dynamic swings, extreme registers, intense dissonances. The emotion of the Verkärte Nacht string sextet is real and uniro

items.name: Brahmsian thematic development
items.description: Despite the Wagnerian harmony, Schoenberg develops his themes in the Brahms manner: motivic cells transformed, fragmented, recombined. This is a specific hybrid.

items.name: Large late-Romantic orchestra
items.description: Enormous orchestral forces (Gurrelieder requires 5 soloists, 3 male choruses, 1 mixed chorus, speaker, and large orchestra).

items.name: Still has a tonal center
items.description: Despite the chromatic intensity, these works always have a key. The tonal center may be distant or delayed, but it exists.
